questions.q: What does an addressing dimension control in a table calculation?
options: The direction the calculation moves through — which cells count as 'before' and 'after'
Whether the field is a dimension or a measure
The color of the pill in the Data pane
Whether the calculation is a table calc or a calculated field
questions.explain: Addressing dimensions determine direction — they decide the order the calculation moves through cells, which matters for things like Running Total and Percent Difference.

questions.q: What does a partitioning dimension control?
options: The scope — it breaks the view into separate sub-tables, and the calculation restarts fresh inside each one
The direction the calculation moves through the view
The exact numeric formula used by the calculation
Whether the field appears on Rows or Columns
questions.explain: Partitioning dimensions break the view into separate scopes — the calculation runs independently within each partition rather than continuously across all of them.

questions.q: In Tableau's Specific Dimensions option, what happens to a dimension you leave unchecked?
options: It becomes a partitioning dimension — the calculation restarts fresh for each of its values
It becomes an addressing dimension automatically
It is removed from the view entirely
Unchecked dimensions are ignored and have no effect on the calculation
questions.explain: Every dimension in the view is either checked (addressing) or unchecked (partitioning) — there's no third option. An unchecked dimension becomes a scope boundary the calculation restarts within.

questions.q: What is Table (Across), in terms of addressing and partitioning?
options: A preset that addresses whatever's on Columns and partitions by whatever's on Rows
A preset that addresses whatever's on Rows and partitions by whatever's on Columns
A setting that has nothing to do with addressing or partitioning
A preset that always partitions by every dimension in the view
questions.explain: Table (Across) addresses the Columns dimension — the calculation moves left to right — and partitions by whatever's on Rows, restarting at the start of each row.

questions.q: How do addressing and partitioning map onto a SQL window function?
options: Partitioning matches PARTITION BY (grouping/scope); addressing matches ORDER BY (the sequence within each group)
Addressing matches PARTITION BY, and partitioning matches ORDER BY
Both map onto the same clause, GROUP BY
There is no relationship between table calculations and SQL window functions
questions.explain: PARTITION BY breaks a SQL result set into groups exactly like Tableau's partitioning dimensions do, while ORDER BY decides the sequence within each group exactly like Tableau's addressing dimensions do.
